events.headline: BMS-Nektar collaboration agreement formally closes; Nektar receives $1.0B upfront plus $850M equity proceeds
events.detail: The Strategic Collaboration Agreement dated February 13, 2018 became effective after Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust clearance; Nektar received the $1.0 billion upfront payment and $850.0 million in share-purchase proceeds on this date, growing cash and investments from $353.2 million at year-end 2017 to $2.1 billion by June 30, 2018.

source.title: Nektar Therapeutics Reports Financial Results for the Second Quarter of 2018 (Form 8-K exhibit)

events.opened_note: Used the Q2 2018 earnings 8-K exhibit, which restates the April 3, 2018 closing and payment amounts, because the original April 2018 closing announcement was not independently located and opened.

events.headline: ASCO 2018 data show PIVOT combination response rates fall as patient cohorts grow beyond the first small groups
events.detail: In the melanoma arm, the objective response rate was 85% in the first 13 evaluable patients but 50% (14/28) once the cohort expanded; in renal-cell carcinoma, the rate was 64% in the first 11 patients but 46% (12/26) in the expanded cohort. Among 283 patients treated at the recommended dose, 14.1% had a Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse event.

source.title: Preliminary Data for NKTR-214 in Combination with Opdivo (nivolumab) for Patients with Stage IV Metastatic Melanoma, Renal Cell Carcinoma, and Urothelial Cancers Presented at ASCO 2018 (Form 8-K exhibit)

events.headline: A short-seller research report questioning NKTR-214's drug-exposure data coincides with a sharp one-day share decline
events.detail: Plainview LLC published a report arguing the clinical dose of NKTR-214 delivers only 7-20% of the active drug exposure of standard IL-2 treatment and comparing the development thesis to a previously disproven immuno-oncology approach; the stock fell sharply the same day, compounding concerns raised by the diminished ASCO response rates reported that summer.
events.opened_note: News source used because the Plainview report itself is not a public company filing; this is market-wide/company-specific commentary, not a primary regulatory or company source.

events.headline: Pension funds file a securities class action alleging Nektar misrepresented NKTR-214 trial data before the BMS deal
events.detail: Two pension funds sued on behalf of investors who purchased Nektar stock between January 10, 2017 and September 28, 2018, alleging the company's promotional "30-fold" efficacy chart drew on data that included an outlier patient result and misrepresented the drug's activity ahead of and after the BMS collaboration.

source.title: In re Nektar Therapeutics: Ninth Circuit Affirms Dismissal of Securities Class Action Arising from Failure of Clinical Drug Trial

events.opened_note: This legal-analysis summary states the complaint was filed in October 2018 without giving the exact calendar day; date approximated to 2018-10-01. The original complaint itself was not independently opened.

events.headline: Updated ASCO 2019 data show the melanoma combination's response and complete-response rates recovering
events.detail: With 12-month follow-up in 38 efficacy-evaluable first-line metastatic melanoma patients, the objective response rate was 53% and the complete-response rate was 34%, with 80% of responses ongoing; the company reported no direct comparison figures for renal-cell carcinoma in this release.

source.title: Nektar Therapeutics Presents Biomarker and Clinical Data from PIVOT-02 Phase 2 Study of Bempegaldesleukin with Nivolumab at 2019 ASCO Annual Meeting

events.headline: Nektar secures up to $150 million in non-dilutive financing from SFJ Pharmaceuticals for a new registrational trial
events.detail: SFJ Pharmaceuticals agreed to fund up to $150 million and manage operations for a new Phase 2/3 registrational study of bempegaldesleukin plus pembrolizumab in PD-L1-positive head and neck cancer, expected to complete in 2024; Nektar's CEO said the deal provided funding to broaden the registrational program without equity dilution.

source.title: Nektar Announces Collaboration with SFJ Pharmaceuticals for Bempegaldesleukin in Head and Neck Cancer

events.headline: Pivotal Phase 3 PIVOT IO-001 trial in melanoma misses its co-primary endpoints against Opdivo alone
events.detail: In 783 previously untreated melanoma patients, the bempegaldesleukin-plus-Opdivo combination did not meet the co-primary endpoints of progression-free survival or objective response rate versus Opdivo monotherapy, and overall survival did not reach statistical significance at the first interim analysis; the companies unblinded the trial and stopped enrollment in the related adjuvant-melanoma study, PIVOT-12, while continuing four other ongoing studies in renal-cell and bladder cancer.

source.title: Bristol Myers Squibb and Nektar Announce Update on Phase 3 PIVOT IO-001 Trial Evaluating Bempegaldesleukin (BEMPEG) in Combination with Opdivo (nivolumab) in Previously Untreated Unresectable or Metastatic Melanoma (Form 8-K exhibit)

events.headline: Nektar and BMS jointly end the entire global bempegaldesleukin-plus-Opdivo development program
events.detail: The companies discontinued all ongoing studies in the combination program, including PIVOT-09 (Phase 3, renal-cell carcinoma), PIVOT-10 (Phase 2, urothelial cancer), and two other studies; an independent Data Monitoring Committee found PIVOT-09's response-rate benefit versus a tyrosine-kinase-inhibitor control did not meet its pre-specified statistical boundary, and PIVOT-10 did not reach its efficacy threshold.

source.title: Nektar and Bristol Myers Squibb Announce Update on Clinical Development Program for Bempegaldesleukin (BEMPEG) in Combination with Opdivo (nivolumab)
source.publisher: PR Newswire (Nektar Therapeutics / Bristol Myers Squibb)

events.headline: Ninth Circuit affirms dismissal of the 2018 securities class action over NKTR-214 data disclosures
events.detail: The appeals court unanimously affirmed the district court's dismissal with prejudice, holding the plaintiffs failed to adequately allege falsity and loss causation regarding the pre-2018 efficacy chart and subsequent disclosures.

source.title: In re Nektar Therapeutics: Ninth Circuit Affirms Dismissal of Securities Class Action Arising from Failure of Clinical Drug Trial

events.opened_note: The Cooley analysis, published after the ruling, gives the May 19, 2022 decision date; the Ninth Circuit opinion itself was not independently opened.

horizon_notes.1: By the one-year mark (2019-02-15), the record shows the BMS collaboration closed on schedule in April 2018 with the promised $1.85 billion in combined upfront and equity proceeds [e1], but the pivotal-trial-readiness data that followed complicated the picture: ASCO 2018 data in June showed response rates roughly halving as the melanoma and renal-cell cohorts grew from a handful of patients to two to three dozen [e2], a short-seller report and a sharp one-day decline followed in October [e3], and a securities class action covering this period was filed the same month [e4]. Interpretation: the packet's flagged catalysts (deal closing, mid-2018 pivotal-study progress) occurred on the guided timeline, but its unresolved question -- whether early uncontrolled response rates would hold up as more patients were added -- received an early, discouraging partial answer within the first year, which the packet could not have shown a reader in advance.
horizon_notes.3: By the three-year mark (2021-02-15), updated 2019 ASCO data showed the melanoma cohort's response and complete-response rates recovering (53% ORR, 34% CR, up from the prior year) [e5], following the 2018 deal closing and the disclosures and litigation that followed it [e1][e2][e3][e4]. Interpretation: through three years, the packet's central question -- whether a large partner's premium mainly reflected confidence in the science or the option value of broad indication access -- remained genuinely open: BMS stayed in the collaboration and the data had stabilized, but no registration-enabling (pivotal, Phase 3) trial had yet read out, so the packet's most consequential uncertainty was still empirically untested at this point.
horizon_notes.5: By the five-year mark (2023-02-15), Nektar had added non-dilutive financing for a further registrational trial via SFJ Pharmaceuticals in February 2021 [e6], but the first pivotal (Phase 3) readout, PIVOT IO-001 in melanoma, missed its co-primary endpoints in March 2022 [e7], leading Nektar and BMS to jointly end the entire global bempegaldesleukin-Opdivo combination program in April 2022 across melanoma, renal-cell, urothelial and other studies [e8]; separately, the Ninth Circuit affirmed dismissal of the 2018 securities litigation in May 2022 [e9]. Interpretation: the packet's central unresolved question -- whether pivotal-scale trials would confirm the early, uncontrolled response rates that justified BMS's premium -- was answered negatively within this window: the first Phase 3 readout failed and the entire combination program with BMS ended, an outcome the packet could flag as a risk (via the field's base rates and the packet's own three unresolved questions) but could not predict.

aftermath.attribution_caveat: Price moves have many causes; the events here are what was public, not a proof of why the price moved.
gaps: The exact calendar day of the October 2018 securities-suit filing (e4) is approximate; only a 2022 secondary legal-analysis summary was opened, not the original complaint.

A January 2020 amendment expanding the BMS-Nektar registrational trial program (from three to five trials, per unopened secondary summaries) is not included as an event: businesswire.com and streetinsider.com pages describing it returned 403 errors, and the one primary source that was opened (a Bristol-Myers Squibb earnings-release exhibit) confirmed only that an amendment occurred in January 2020 without stating its substance, which was judged too thin to support a standalone event with confident detail.
ir.nektar.com press-release pages timed out repeatedly and could not be opened directly; SEC EDGAR filings and PR Newswire/BioSpace wire copies were used instead where available.

This timeline focuses on the NKTR-214/bempegaldesleukin catalysts flagged in the pre-cutoff packet; it does not cover the royalty business (AstraZeneca's Movantik, Baxalta/Shire's Adynovate) or Nektar's post-2023 pipeline pivot toward immunology and rezpegaldesleukin, which falls outside the five-year window.

No macro-context event is included: a search for 2022 sector-wide biotech-downturn commentary tied specifically to Nektar did not surface a source that both discussed sector-wide conditions and was independently verifiable within budget; the company-specific trial failures (e7, e8) are treated as the dominant explanation instead.

scene_check.voice: A major pharma has agreed to put $1 billion into a partnership with them and to buy $850 million of their stock at a premium. They're backing this cancer treatment while it's still in early trials. That makes me interested. What do you think?

claims.text: a $1 billion cash payment plus an $850 million equity purchase at a premium, agreed and pending closing
the candidate is still in early trials: a 38-patient uncontrolled dose-escalation study
the friend's inference: a big partner's backing makes it interesting (not a reported fact)

debrief_check.s1: The agreement closed on 3 April 2018 after antitrust clearance, and the cash and equity proceeds were received as agreed [e1].
debrief_check.s2: Early it was. As the melanoma and kidney cohorts grew past the first handful of patients in June 2018, response rates were roughly half the initial figures; twelve-month data in 2019 showed them recovering; the first randomised Phase 3, 783 patients, missed both co-primary endpoints in March 2022 [e2][e5][e7].
debrief_check.s3: The partner did commit the money and stayed in the programme for four years [e1][e6][e8]. What the backing could not tell anyone in February 2018 was whether the drug worked; the record says it did not, and that took a Phase 3 to establish.

assumptions.text: The early clinical results will hold up as more patients are treated.
The partnership removes the financing risk for years.
The current valuation still leaves enough upside if the drug works.
I don't have enough evidence to take a position either way.
The price already assumes success; the risk is to the downside.

thesis_check.a1: Evidence: response rates fell by roughly half as cohorts grew (June 2018), recovered in twelve-month data (2019), and the first randomised Phase 3 missed both co-primary endpoints (March 2022) [e2][e5][e7]. For this assumption: not supported over the full record; within the first year the evidence had already weakened it. Unknown: whether a different dose or population would have fared better; the programme ended before that was tested.
thesis_check.a2: Evidence: the $1 billion and the $850 million equity were received in April 2018, the partner stayed until April 2022, and a further financing of up to $150 million was agreed in 2021 [e1][e6][e8]. For this assumption: supported; no financing crisis appears in the record. Unknown: how much of the $150 million was drawn, and what the company's cash position was at each date, which this record does not collect.
thesis_check.a3: Evidence: the stock fell sharply within months of the cutoff and the drug later failed; see the result tiles for the return over the horizon you chose [e2][e3][e7]. For this assumption: it was never put to the test, because the condition 'if the drug works' did not occur. Unknown: what the upside would have been on success; a failed drug does not show that the earlier price already assumed success.
thesis_check.a4: Evidence: the packet itself said the data came from 38 uncontrolled patients, and the decisive Phase 3 read out four years after the cutoff [e7]. For this assumption: consistent with how the record unfolded; nothing decisive arrived for years. Unknown: a wait can also miss a winner; this record happens not to be one.
thesis_check.a5: Evidence: no event in the record added to the story the price told in February 2018; the expanded data, the short report, the litigation and the Phase 3 each subtracted from it, with the 2019 recovery as the exception [e2][e3][e4][e5][e7]. For this assumption: broadly supported, with that exception. Unknown: how much of the decline was the drug and how much the wider biotech market; this record does not separate them.

event.headline: ASCO 2018 data show PIVOT combination response rates fall as patient cohorts grow beyond the first small groups
event.detail: In the melanoma arm, the objective response rate was 85% in the first 13 evaluable patients but 50% (14/28) once the cohort expanded; in renal-cell carcinoma, the rate was 64% in the first 11 patients but 46% (12/26) in the expanded cohort. Among 283 patients treated at the recommended dose, 14.1% had a Grade 3+ treatment-related adverse event.

walkthrough.stage_text: Two months after the deal closed, expanded data are shown at the big oncology meeting. The melanoma response rate, 85% in the first 13 patients, is 50% once the cohort reaches 28; the kidney cohort shows the same pattern. Nothing has failed and the partner is still in. But the small-sample response rates the pitch rested on have moved.

event.headline: Updated ASCO 2019 data show the melanoma combination's response and complete-response rates recovering
event.detail: With 12-month follow-up in 38 efficacy-evaluable first-line metastatic melanoma patients, the objective response rate was 53% and the complete-response rate was 34%, with 80% of responses ongoing; the company reported no direct comparison figures for renal-cell carcinoma in this release.

walkthrough.stage_text: A year on, with twelve months of follow-up in 38 first-line melanoma patients, the response rate is 53% with 34% complete responses, better than the previous year's expanded read. In the meantime a short-seller report questioned the drug's exposure data and a securities class action was filed; both are unresolved at this point. Pivotal trials are running. The question is unchanged: will this hold in a randomised trial of hundreds?

event.headline: Pivotal Phase 3 PIVOT IO-001 trial in melanoma misses its co-primary endpoints against the partner's drug alone
event.detail: In 783 previously untreated melanoma patients, the the candidate-plus-the partner's drug combination did not meet the co-primary endpoints of progression-free survival or objective response rate versus the partner's drug monotherapy, and overall survival did not reach statistical significance at the first interim analysis; the companies unblinded the trial and stopped enrollment in the related adjuvant-melanoma study, PIVOT-12, while continuing four other ongoing studies in renal-cell and bladder cancer.

walkthrough.stage_text: The first Phase 3, 783 untreated melanoma patients, misses both co-primary endpoints against the partner's drug alone. The other combination studies are still running as of this date; what the companies will do with them is not yet announced.

event.headline: the company and the partner jointly end the entire global the candidate-plus-the partner's drug development program
event.detail: The companies discontinued all ongoing studies in the combination program, including PIVOT-09 (Phase 3, renal-cell carcinoma), PIVOT-10 (Phase 2, urothelial cancer), and two other studies; an independent Data Monitoring Committee found PIVOT-09's response-rate benefit versus a tyrosine-kinase-inhibitor control did not meet its pre-specified statistical boundary, and PIVOT-10 did not reach its efficacy threshold.

walkthrough.stage_text: A month later the two companies end the entire combination programme across every indication. The partnership's clinical bet is over; the cash and equity paid in 2018 are not returned.
